candidate.answerReason: In quarter-quart units, the millet amount after each refill follows m_next=(3/4)m+1, while the other seeds always total 3 units. The millet first exceeds 3 units on Friday.

methods.label: Track the millet after each refill
methods.explanation:
Measure seed amounts in units of \(\tfrac14\) quart. Each new quart adds \(1\) unit of millet and \(3\) units of other seeds. Since the birds eat all the other seeds each day, just after every refill there are exactly \(3\) units of other seeds. Millet is more than half the total precisely when its amount exceeds these \(3\) units.

Let \(m_n\) be the millet amount just after the \(n\)th refill, with \(n=1\) on Monday. The birds leave \(\tfrac34\) of the millet, and the next refill adds \(1\) unit, so
\[
m_1=1,\qquad m_{n+1}=\frac34m_n+1.
\]
For example, Tuesday's amount is \(\tfrac34(1)+1=\tfrac74\). Continuing the same calculation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Monday: }&1,\\
\text{Tuesday: }&\frac74,\\
\text{Wednesday: }&\frac{37}{16},\\
\text{Thursday: }&\frac{175}{64},\\
\text{Friday: }&\frac{781}{256}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The amounts through Thursday are all below \(3\); in particular, \(\tfrac{175}{64}<\tfrac{192}{64}=3\). Friday's amount satisfies \(\tfrac{781}{256}>\tfrac{768}{256}=3\). Therefore the first such day is \(\boxed{\text{Friday}}\), choice D.
methods.levelReason: The recurrence records a simple daily retention-and-addition rule. Five exact arithmetic steps settle the question without a general sequence formula.

methods.label: Track the shortfall from a reference amount
methods.explanation:
Use units of \(\tfrac14\) quart. Each refill adds \(1\) unit of millet and \(3\) units of other seeds. Just after a refill, all other seeds from earlier days have been eaten, so millet must exceed \(3\) units to make up more than half the seeds.

A useful reference amount is \(4\) units of millet: eating one-quarter leaves \(3\), and adding \(1\) restores \(4\). Track the shortfall from this reference. If the millet amount after a refill is \(4-d\), then after the birds eat and the next refill occurs, it becomes
\[
\frac34(4-d)+1=4-\frac34d.
\]
Thus the shortfall is multiplied by \(\tfrac34\) each day. On Monday the millet amount is \(1\), so the shortfall is \(3\).

Millet exceeds \(3\) units exactly when its shortfall from \(4\) is less than \(1\). On Thursday the shortfall is
\[
3\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac34
=\frac{81}{64}>1.
\]
On Friday it is
\[
\frac{81}{64}\cdot\frac34
=\frac{243}{256}<1.
\]
The positive shortfall decreases each day, so every day before Thursday also has shortfall greater than \(1\). The first qualifying day is therefore \(\boxed{\text{Friday}}\), choice D.
methods.levelReason: The reference amount turns the daily rule into repeated fraction multiplication using only distributivity and comparison, with no geometric-series formula.

Both methods use percentage amounts, fraction multiplication, and comparison. The main route adds unlike fractions; the alternative uses distributivity and a stable reference amount to obtain a multiplicative shortfall rule. These method-specific steps remain local. No general-term formula or probability recursion is required.
